body:
Ok thanks for the explanation !
I was not asking for a workaround, because I think one shouldn't have to modify its code for static analysis :)

I got deeper in phpstan understanding and I think this will be really ~a mess~ challenging to add complement types, especially methods that add/remove/union/intersect types !

> I was not asking for a workaround, because I think one shouldn't have to modify its code for static analysis :)

This isn't true - you can benefit from improving your code because it will be understandable better not only by a static analyser, but also by other developers. So adding typehints and simplifying code for better readability is a win-win for everyone.

> challenging to add complement types, especially methods that add/remove/union/intersect types

I don't think so, the typesystem is quite ready for it. But I'm not asking you to do this work, it must be done by someone familiar with the core.
Well I can't wait for this :) Thanks for all :heart:
@paxal You can read this to learn how to maximize the benefits static analysis can offer you 😊 https://www.phparch.com/2018/04/testing-strategy-with-the-help-of-static-analysis/

If anyone encounters this issue : https://phpstan.org/r/b22ce1c7-f219-47b3-8d33-e029a579748e
It can be fixed by replacing to `@var \Traversable<...>` : https://phpstan.org/r/bf512221-3676-435d-ba82-b49f16725978
@gnutix iterable is `Traversable|array`, and `array` cannot be passed to `iterator_to_array`.
This thread has been automatically locked since there has not been any recent activity after it was closed. Please open a new issue for related bugs.
